Sec. 901. 
Section 5545a of title 5, United States Code, is amended—

(1) 
in subsection (a)(2)—

(A) 
in the matter before subparagraph (A) by striking “is required to” and inserting in lieu thereof “who is required to”; and


(B) 
by inserting “and” immediately after subparagraph (E)(v); and



(2) 
by adding at the end thereof the following new subsection:


“(j) 
Notwithstanding any other provision of this section, any Office of Inspector General which employs fewer than 5 criminal investigators may elect not to cover such criminal investigators under this section.”.






Sec. 902. 

(a) 
Section 5545a of title 5, United States Code, is amended by inserting at the appropriate place the following new subsection:


“(i) 
The provisions of subsections (a)–(h) providing for availability pay shall apply to a pilot employed by the United States Customs Service who is a law enforcement officer as defined under section 5541(3). For the purpose of this section, section 5542(d) of this title, and section 13(a)(16) and (b)(30) of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 (29 U.S.C. 213(a)(16) and (b)(30)), such pilot shall be deemed to be a criminal investigator as defined in this section. The Office of Personnel Management may prescribe regulations to carry out this subsection.”.





(b) 

The amendment made by subsection (a) of this section shall take effect on the first day of the first applicable pay period which begins on or after the 30th day following the date of enactment of this Act.



Sec. 903. 

Section 528 of Public Law 103–329 is amended by adding at the end a new proviso: “Provided further, That the amount set forth therefor in the budget estimates may be exceeded by no more than 5 percent in the event of emergency requirements.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is "No", because the section deals only with internal federal pay matters (availability pay for criminal investigators and Customs pilots) and names no outside party. However, it authorizes OPM to prescribe regulations, and under the definition a grant of rulemaking authority counts as participation even when it is discretionary ("may"), since rulemaking brings in public comment. The rest of the section contains no participation mechanism, so the label rests on this one sentence.
fable.s: The Office of Personnel Management may prescribe regulations to carry out this subsection.

The tempting reading treats the section as purely internal federal pay administration, but that ignores the rulemaking grant. The other provisions involve no outside parties.

1. **The tempting-but-wrong reading:** This is a set of internal personnel and pay amendments (availability pay for federal criminal investigators and Customs pilots, plus a budget proviso). Every actor named is federal: Offices of Inspector General, the Customs Service, and OPM. On that view, nothing crosses the federal boundary. However, Sec. 902 gives OPM authority to issue regulations. Under the DEFINITION ("requiring rulemaking") and Worked Example 6, a grant of rulemaking authority counts as participation even when it is optional ("may"), because rulemaking brings in public notice and comment.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends provisions regarding federal employee pay and benefits (specifically for criminal investigators and Customs Service pilots) and budget estimates. It does not require or recommend consultation with, or participation by, any parties outside the federal government. The Office of Personnel Management is a federal agency, and its authority to prescribe regulations is an internal administrative function not described here as involving public input.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) prescribing regulations implies a rulemaking process that could involve public comment. However, the text itself does not mandate public participation in that rulemaking, nor does it describe any other form of consultation with outside parties. The section primarily deals with internal federal employment classifications, pay provisions, and budgetary adjustments. All actors mentioned (Inspectors General, Customs Service pilots, OPM, Congress) are inside the federal government.
